changes.text: 还有一处值得注意（作者的解读）：停下之后，他们反而能一趟趟回到沉船附近，捞回衣物、食物和少数私人物品；沙克尔顿后来说，那些私人物品当初是怀着“轻松的乐观”，才打算在冲过移动冰面奔向安全时丢在几英里之外的。他还决定让大家几乎全靠海豹和企鹅过活，把雪橇口粮留给后面的小艇航行。作者认为，停下不只是不再消耗，也是把资源重新收拢的时间。

One more thing is worth noticing, and again it is the author's reading. Once they stopped, they could go back to the wreck again and again and retrieve clothing, food and some few articles of personal value; Shackleton later said it was in "light-hearted optimism" that they had thought to leave those articles miles behind on their dash across the moving ice to safety. He also decided they would live almost entirely on seals and penguins so that the sledging rations could be kept for the boat journey ahead. On this reading, stopping was not only a halt to the drain; it was time to gather their resources again.
文本是 OCR，有讹字，引用只取清晰片段，个别有讹字的词不加引号照抄。主要数字——1800英里、281天、346英里、两磅、一吨、一英里、六英里、一英里半、两个月、三个半月——都出自他的记述，未与别的记录核对。本篇也不写耐心营之后的经过，那部分不在这份证据包的覆盖范围内。

The text is machine-read, and it carries errors. Quotations are taken only from clean stretches; a few damaged words are reproduced without quotation marks. The main figures — 1,800 miles, 281 days, 346 miles, two pounds, a ton, one mile, six miles, one and a half miles, two months, three and a half months — come from his account and have not been checked against any other record. Nor does this piece tell what happened after Patience Camp; that falls outside the evidence gathered here.
全部来自沙克尔顿本人的叙述（本篇用1920年印本的 OCR 文本），是当事人、领导者的记述，没有其他队员的日记作对照；OCR 有讹字，引用只取清晰片段；文中数字均出自该记述，未经独立核对；本篇不涉及耐心营之后的经过。

Everything here comes from Shackleton's own narrative (this piece uses the OCR text of the 1920 printing): the account of the participant who led the party, with no other member's diary for comparison. The OCR carries errors, and quotations are drawn only from clean stretches. Every figure in the piece comes from that account and has not been independently verified. What happened after Patience Camp is not covered here.
